703083.t: Contraction of γαῖα (gaîă), from Proto-Hellenic *gaya, from a pre-Indo-European Pre-Greek substrate.

703051.t: From γέννα (génna) + -άω (-ắō), poetic form of γένος (génos, “offspring”). Causal counterpart of γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to be born, to become”).

703043.t: From Proto-Hellenic *génetis, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵénh₁tis. Synchronically, a verbal noun from γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to come into being”) + -σις (-sĭs).

703037.t: Formally it would be from Proto-Hellenic *genehā́, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁eseh₂, feminine derivation from *ǵénh₁os (whence γένος (génos)), from *ǵenh₁-. Compare εἶδος (eîdos) - ἰδέα (idéa).

703057.t: From Proto-Hellenic *génos. Cognate with Latin genus, Sanskrit जनस् (jánas), Old Armenian ծին (cin), among others; see also γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to be born”).

703054.t: From γεννάω (gennắō, “I beget”) + -σις (-sĭs, verbal noun suffix). Compare simple γένεσις (génesis).

703075.t: Compare Old Armenian կամուրջ (kamurǰ, “bridge”) and Hattic 𒄩𒄠𒈬𒊒𒊀 (ḫa-am-mu-ru-waₐ /⁠ḫamuruwa, ḫammuruwa, ḫāmuruwaₐ⁠/, “beam”), with further origin unknown.

703074.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵews-. Cognates include Old English ċēosan (English choose), Latin gustō,, Sanskrit जुषते (juṣate).

703065.t: From Proto-Hellenic *géronts, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵérh₂onts (“old”). Cognates include Sanskrit जर॑त् (járat, “old man”), Old Armenian ծերուն (cerun), and Middle Irish gérat (“champion”).

703046.t: From γένος (génos, “race, stock, kin”) + -ικός (-ĭkós, adjectival suffix).

703019.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵelh₂- (“to laugh”) (which Beekes incorrectly reconstructs as *gelh₂-). Cognates include Old Armenian ծաղր (całr, “laughter”).

703063.t: Ultimately from γέρων (gérōn, “old man”). Related to Mycenaean Greek 𐀐𐀫𐀯𐀊 (ke-ro-si-ja)

703016.t: Beekes does not propose an etymology, and leaves its origin open, though notes that the seemingly-old ablaut in the suffix -των (-tōn) suggests ultimate Indo-European origin.

703061.t: Perhaps originally "privilege of age", from Proto-Indo-European *ǵerh₂- (“to grow old”). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀐𐀨 (ke-ra).

703040.t: From Proto-Hellenic *génewyom, from the root of γένυς (génŭs, “jaw, mouth”).

703048.t: From γέννα (génna, “descent, birth, origin”) + -ιος (-ios). Compare ἀγενής (agenḗs).

703089.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵērh₂-s, a lengthened-grade derivative of *ǵerh₂- (“to grow old”). Cognate with Sanskrit जरा (jarā́, “old age”).

703039.t: Probably derived from γένεθλον (génethlon) or γενέθλη (genéthlē, “race, stock, family, birthplace”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁- (“to give birth”) + *-dʰlom (“instrumental suffix”). See also γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to be born”).

703044.t: From the root of γίγνομαι (gĭ́gnomai, “to be born”) from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-.

703036.t: Probably Proto-Hellenic *gémō, from Proto-Indo-European *gém-e-ti, a simple thematic present belonging to the root *gem- (“to take, seize”).
